label: mainthm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{mainthm} Let $S^{G^{\infty}}(M)$ be the regular diffeological Lie group of super symplectic diffeomorphisms of a supermanifold $M$.                                                               
$S^{G^{\infty}}(M)$is a Lie subgroup of the group of super diffeomorphisms $D^{G^{\infty}}(M)$; further, there exist induced representations for Hilbert space representations for these two regular Lie groups.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $X$ be a set. An $n$-parametrization of $X$ is defined as a map $f : U \rightarrow X$, where $U$ is an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{n}, n\ge 0$. A constant parametrization is a map of the form $f : U\rightarrow X$ such that $f(u) = x$ for all $u \in U$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $X$ be a set and $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of parametrizations on $X$. The diffeology on $X$ induced by $\mathcal{F}$ is the intersection of all diffeologies on $X$ containing $\mathcal{F}$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $(X,\mathcal {F})$ and $(Y,\mathcal{G})$ be diffeological spaces. A map $f:X\rightarrow Y$ is \emph{smooth} if $f$ takes plots of the diffeology on $X$ to plots of the diffeology on $Y$.

title: Definition
body_md:
A difeological space $(S,F)$ is \emph{lattice type} (or \emph{L-type}) when given any two plots $f:M_1 
 \rightarrow S$, $g:M_2 \rightarrow S$ 
 at a point $f(x) = g(y)$, there exists a third plot $h$ through which the germs of $f$ at $x$ and $g$ 
 at $y$ factor, that is there exists a map $h:N 
 \rightarrow S$ with $f = h\circ \varphi$, $g=h\circ \gamma$ where $\varphi: \tilde{M_1} \rightarrow N
 $ and $\gamma: \tilde{M_2} 
 \rightarrow N$ are plots such that $\tilde{M_i} \subset M_i$, $i=1,2$ are neigborhoods of $x$ and $y$ 
 respectively and $\varphi(x) = \gamma(y)$.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $V$ and $W$ be topological graded modules over $\Gamma_{0}$ and let $U\subseteq V$ be open in $V$. A function $f: U \rightarrow W$ will be called supersmoooth or $G^{\infty}$ when for every $n\ge 1$, there exist continuous maps which are regular $k$-multimorphisms in the k terminal variables for each fixed $x \in U$, denoted by $D^{k}f(x;\cdots): U \times V \times \cdots \times V \rightarrow W$, where $k \le n$, such that the map
\[
F_{k}(h):=f(x+h)-f(x)-Df(x;h)-\frac{1}{2!}D^{2}f(x;h,h) - \cdots - \frac{1}{k!}D^{k}f(x;h,\dots h), 1\le k \le n
\] 
satisfies the property that

\[
G_{k}(t,h) := \left\{\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{F_{k}(th)}{t^{k}}, & t \ne 0 \\
0, & t = 0 \end{array}\right.
\]
is continuous at $(0,h)$ in $V$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
$\mathfrak{D}$ is closed under coproducts. For a collection $\{X_{i}|i\in I\}$ of 
diffeological spaces, the coproduct of the collection is called the \emph{sum} of the diffeological spaces $X_{i}$ and is denoted $\displaystyle \sqcup_{i\in I}X_{i}$ (Iglesias \cite{Igl}, 1.39).
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $\mathfrak{D}$ is closed under products. Just as in the above result, given an arbitrary collection $\{X_{i}|i\in I\}$, the product object is denoted $\displaystyle \prod_{i\in I}X_{i}$ and can be given a canonical diffeology (Iglesias \cite{Igl}, 1.55).
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $\mathfrak{D}$ is a symmetric monoidal category.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The product map is derived from the definition of the product object. In addition, since $\mathfrak{D}$ is essentially a concrete category, associativity of the product map holds. We can take any one-point set as a unit object, since all one-point sets are unique up to isomorphism of diffeological spaces (all plots are constant). The coherence axioms are clearly satisfied. The symmetry of $\mathfrak{D}$ is given by the canonical map $\gamma : X \times Y \rightarrow Y \times X, (x,y)\mapsto (y,x)$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $\mathfrak{D}$ is complete with respect to (all small) limits and colimits.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From Mac Lane (\cite{Mac}, Corollary V.2.2), we know that 
if a category $\mathcal{C}$ has equalizers of all pairs of arrows and all small products, then $\mathcal{C}$ is small-complete. In $\mathfrak{D}$, the equalizer of pairs of smooth maps $f,g: X \rightarrow Y$ is defined to be the subspace $Z$ of $X$ such that $f(x) = g(x)$ for $x\in Z$. The universal arrow is the canonical inclusion map. The coequalizer is defined for pairs $f,g : X \rightarrow Y$ by considering the smallest equivalence relation $E \subset Y \times Y$ containing all pairs $(f(x), g(x))$, for $x \in X$. The coequalizer is the quotient space $Z = Y/E$, with the universal arrow given by the canonical projection map. From the existence of equalizers, coequalizers, coproducts and products, we conclude that $\mathfrak{D}$ is complete.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $\mathfrak{D}$ is Cartesian closed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The map $\phi :\mathfrak{D}(X\times Y, Z) \rightarrow \mathfrak{D}(X, \mathfrak{D}(Y,Z))$ given by $(\phi(f)(x))(y) = f(x,y)$ for $f: X\times Y \rightarrow Z$ is a bijection, and shows that the functor $\mathfrak{D}(Y,-): \mathfrak{D} \rightarrow \mathfrak{D}$ is the right adjoint to the functor $- \times Y:\mathfrak{D} \rightarrow \mathfrak{D}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The properties of $\mathfrak{D}$ as a category make it suitable as an enriching category. This gives us the ability to use the results of Kelly \cite{Kel} on indexed limits, indexed colimits and Kan extensions in the case of enriched categories. These ideas are discussed in the following section.

title: Definition
body_md: $D^{G^{\infty}}(M)$ is defined to be the group of super diffeomorphisms of $M$, where $M$ is a supermanifold. $D^{G^{\infty}}(M)$ can be made into a diffeological space by applying the \emph{function space diffeology:} a map $f: U \subseteq D^{G^{\infty}}(M)$ is a plot if the induced map $F : U \times M \rightarrow M$ given by $F(u,m) = (f(u))(m)$ is smooth for all $u \in U$. The smallest diffeology generated by such plots is called the function space diffeology on $D^{G^{\infty}}(M)$.

label: natend
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{natend} Let $F,G : \mathcal{J} \rightarrow \mathfrak{D}$ be smooth functors. Then $\{
F,G\} \simeq Nat(F,G)$, the diffeological space of natural transformations between the functors $F$ and $G$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the fact that the space of natural transformations between $F$ and $G$ can be expressed as an \emph{end}: $Nat(F,G) \simeq \int_c \mathfrak{D}(Fc, Gc)$. Using the language of ends, we obtain the following isomorphisms:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak{D}(c, \{F,G\}) & \simeq \mathfrak{D}^{\mathcal{J}}(F, \mathfrak{D}(c,G-)) = Nat(F, D(c, G-))\\
 	&\simeq \int_x \mathfrak{D}(Fx, D(c,Gx)) \\
	& \simeq \mathfrak{D}\left( c, \int_x \mathfrak{D}(Fx, Gx)\right) = \mathfrak{D}(c, Nat(F,G))\\
\end{aligned} 
\]
Therefore $\{F,G\}$ is isomorphic to $Nat(F,G)$.

\label{leftkanexists}
Let $K: \mathcal{M} \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}$ and $T: \mathcal{M} \longrightarrow \mathcal{A}$ be smooth functors of diffeological categories. The left Kan extension of $T$ along $K$ is given by the functor $L: \mathcal{C}\rightarrow \mathcal{A}$, given by $Lc = \mathcal{C}(K-,c) * T$, whenever it exists.

title: Proof
body_md:
Given a representation $T: \mathcal{H} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$, define the inclusion functor $I : \mathcal{H} \rightarrow \mathcal{G}$. The functor $T : \mathcal{H} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$ is a representation of $\mathcal{H}$. The left Kan extension $L : \mathcal{G} \rightarrow C$ takes the form $L(\mathcal{G}) = \textrm{Hom}(I-,G) \ast T)$, which exists by the proof of the previous theorem, and the completeness of the category $\mathfrak{D}$. Given a representation $S: \mathcal{G} \rightarrow \mathcal{C}$, the composite $SI$ is the restriction of the representation to $\mathcal{H}$. 

The adjunction can therefore be expressed $Nat(L,S)  \simeq Nat(T, SI)$. Let $V = T(\mathcal{H})$ be an $\mathcal{H}$-module, and $W$ a $\mathcal{G}$-module. Denoting $L(G)$ by $I\cdot V$, we obtain the isomorphism (of diffeological spaces)  
\[
\textrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{G}}(I\cdot V, W) \simeq \textrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{H}}(V, W)
\]
establishing that $I\cdot V$ is the (co) induced representation of $\mathcal{G}$.

title: Remark
body_md: The definition of diffeological category raises a question; are there examples of categories with the objects not necessarily diffeological spaces, such that the hom-sets have the structure of a diffeological space? It seems that the underlying structures would need to have the structure of a diffeological space, so we can use the function space diffeology. This means that the category $\mathfrak{D}$ is its own higher-category: for $G, H$ diffeological spaces, the morphism $\mathfrak{D}(G,H)$ is also a diffeological space. We can extend this to $2$-morphisms and so on.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Milnor discusses the issue of regularity of (infinite dimensional) Lie groups in \cite{Mil}. Essentially, a Lie group is regular if there exists an exponential map from the Lie algebra to the Lie group, relating representations of both the algebra and the group. In this paper, we have discussed diffeological Lie groups, and it is natural to ask whether they are regular. J-P. Magnot \cite{Mag} has shown that this is not the case, so not all diffeological Lie groups are regular. This leads to the question whether all regular diffeological Lie groups can be classified.
